thread.title: Here are the hottest Bay Area startups from Q2

author: Cromwell Schubarth
title: Here are the hottest Bay Area startups from Q2
text: – TechFlash Editor, Silicon Valley Business Journal Jul 20, 2018, 11:23am PDT Updated Jul 20, 2018, 12:33pm PDT It seems somehow appropriate that a startup whose app helps people deal with these stressful times is the hottest Bay Area startup from the second quarter. The valuation of Calm.com Inc., a San Francisco company with a meditation app, jumped nearly 43-fold to $277 million when it raised a Series A round last month, according to PitchBook Data. “The period after the election was an anxiety-inducing time and we saw an uptick in the use of the app,” co-founder Alex Tew told the San Francisco Business Times . “Calm’s growth is a reflection of a general increase anxiety and the stresses of modern life.” Of course, it didn't hurt to be named iPhone App of the Year for 2017 by Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL). Calm's big valuation jump topped all of the others on PitchBook's quarterly ranking by a lot. The list only included venture-backed companies whose value is now $100 million or more and jumped by at least fourfold with their most recent round. PitchBook said that the average valuation jump for Bay Area companies that won funding in the last quarter was 2.5X. One of the companies on the second quarter ranking saw a big jump after it raised a big round just two months before going public. Another is a unicorn company whose valuation jumped fourfold despite already being figured to be worth more than $1 billion. Look through the accompanying photo gallery to see all of the companies that made PitchBook's hottest company ranking from the Bay Area for Q2.
